name: Pemphigus Foliaceus

ethnicAssociations: More common in individuals of Mediterranean and South American descent

criteria.description: Superficial erosions and crusted plaques predominantly on seborrheic areas without mucosal involvement
Subcorneal acantholysis with superficial epidermal blister formation on skin biopsy
Intercellular IgG and C3 deposits in the upper epidermis on direct immunofluorescence
Presence of circulating anti-desmoglein 1 autoantibodies detected by ELISA

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical clinical features plus histopathological and immunofluorescence confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Mucosal involvement is absent, distinguishing it from pemphigus vulgaris.

laboratory: Detection of circulating anti-desmoglein 1 IgG autoantibodies by ELISA
Elevated inflammatory markers in secondary infection
genetic: Association with HLA-DRB1*0102 and HLA-DQB1*0503 alleles in some populations
other: Direct immunofluorescence showing intercellular IgG and C3 deposits in upper epidermis

distinguishingFeatures: Mucosal involvement present in pemphigus vulgaris
Deeper suprabasal blister formation in pemphigus vulgaris
Anti-desmoglein 3 autoantibodies predominant in pemphigus vulgaris
Linear IgG and C3 deposits along basement membrane zone on immunofluorescence

redFlags: Signs of secondary bacterial infection (fever, purulence)
Extensive skin involvement causing fluid loss or electrolyte imbalance
references: Bystryn JC, Rudolph JL. Pemphigus. Lancet. 2005;366(9479):61-73.
Harman KE, et al. British Association of Dermatologists' guidelines for the management of pemphigus vulgaris 2017. Br J Dermatol. 2017;177(5):1170-1201.
Lever WF. Pemphigus foliaceus. Arch Dermatol Syphilol. 1957;75(1):1-15.
